provider_response.description:
Represents payout error codes. The `type` and `code` fields are separate enums where:
- `type` indicates the nature of the error.
- `code` provides the specific error code associated with the error type.
- `message` explains the meaning of the `type-code` pair

message.description: The processor message for the transfer.

type.description: The type of the payout error, representing the specific error scenario.

code.description: The unique code associated with the error type. This code follows a pattern of four digits.

reference.description: A custom identifier to track the transaction, This must be unique across all your transactions.

response_schema.description: Return HTTP 200 within 60 seconds; Flutterwave ignores the response body and headers.

gotchas: Signature: Docs (Webhooks): "Flutterwave uses the secret hash you specify on your dashboard to hash the webhook response using `HMAC-SHA256`." The value arrives in the flutterwave-signature header; the documented sample computes createHmac('sha256', secretHash).update(rawBody).digest('base64'). Use the raw body and a constant-time compare. Open question: the same page's framework examples (Node, PHP, Python) instead compare the header directly with the secret hash; follow the signing section and confirm with resend_webhook in sandbox. The secret hash is the one you set in Dashboard → Settings → Webhooks (env FLUTTERWAVE_WEBHOOK_SECRET); it is not an API key.

Respond fast: "your endpoint **must** return a `200` HTTP status code"; "Webhook requests time out after **60 seconds**." Retries: "Be sure to enable webhook retries on your dashboard." — "we'll retry the webhook call **3 times**, with a **30-minute** interval between each attempt."

"Occasionally, we might send the same webhook event more than once." Deduplicate on webhook_id (the API reference requires it on every event; the webhooks page sample shows `id` instead, so read webhook_id ?? id), and record an event as processed only after the work succeeded.

Status casing differs by event: charge.completed / refund.completed use lowercase (succeeded, failed…), transfer.disburse / transfer.reversal use uppercase SUCCESSFUL / FAILED. The customer id is data.customer.id (no data.customer_id). timestamp is Unix epoch milliseconds in every sample. data.created_datetime is an ISO string in the API reference but an epoch float in the webhooks page sample: accept both.
Never fulfil on the webhook alone: Docs (Webhooks): "always re-query our API to verify the transaction details." (get_charge, get_transfer, get_refund).

order.authorization (card pre-authorisation orders) also exists but is out of scope here. Missed a delivery? resend_webhook (POST /resend-webhook {id, type}). "Web frameworks like Rails or Django check POST requests for `CSRF` tokens": exempt this route.
